texts.facts: The facts in brief, necessary for the disposal of the present suit for Recovery of Rs. 6,26,620/-(Rupees six lacs twenty six thousand six hundred and twenty only) filed by the plaintiff, as disclosed in CS DJ 58498/2016 M/s Jupitor Polytex(India) Pvt. Ltd. Vs. M/s Lotus Dairy Products Pvt. Ltd. Page No. 1 of 18 the plaint , are that the plaintiff is a company duly incorporated under the Company's Act, 1956. It has been further stated that vide resolution dated 07.11.2013, Sh. Vijender Singhal, who is one of the directors of the plaintiff company, has been authorized to sign, verify and institute the present suit on behalf of the plaintiff. It has been further stated that the defendants no. 2 to 4 are the directors of defendant no. 1 and they are handling the day to day affairs of defendant no. 1. 2. The plaintiff, in the plaint, has further stated that it supplied multi- layer film material on credit basis to the defendants by way of invoice no. 019 dated 27.4.2011 for an amount of Rs. 57,269/- and vide invoice no. 077 dated 05.07.2011 for an amount of Rs. 1,08,221/-. Ltd on 5 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51885869/ 1 It has been further stated that the defendants received the materials qua the above said two invoices without any complaint. It has been further stated that the plaintiff also supplied the material to the defendants vide bill no. 0176 dated 26.09.2011 for an amount of Rs. 2,29,542/- as per the order of the defendants and the defendants acknowledged the receipt of the goods. It has been further stated that thus, the plaintiff supplied the goods to the defendant for a total amount of Rs. 3,95,032/-. 3. It has been further stated that the defendants reported to the plaintiff that there was some problem in the materials supplied by the plaintiff vide bill dated 26.09.2011 and the plaintiff, immediately upon receipt of the above said information, attended CS DJ 58498/2016 M/s Jupitor Polytex(India) Pvt. Ltd. Vs. M/s Lotus Dairy Products Pvt. Ltd. Page No. 2 of 18 the above said complaint and found that there was no defect in the goods supplied by the plaintiff. It has been further stated that as per the statement of accounts, the plaintiff is liable to pay the principal amount of Rs. 3,95,032/-, an amount of Rs. 2,19,737/- as interest @ 21% per annum w.e.f. 27.05.2011 to 15.12.2013 and an amount of Rs. 11,851/- on account of costs of C-Form totalling to Rs. 6,26,620/-. The plaintiff has further stated that the plaintiff served the legal notice dated 12.09.2013 upon the defendants and the defendants sent a false and frivolous reply dated 30.09.2013 to the legal notice of the plaintiff but the defendants failed to make the above said payment and hence, the present suit. 4. On the basis of the above said allegations as contained in the plaint, the plaintiff has prayed for a decree for a sum of Rs. 6,26,620/-(Rupees six lacs twenty six thousand six hundred and twenty only) together with the pendente-lite and future interest @ 21% per annum. The plaintiff has also prayed for the costs of the suit. 5. Written statement has been filed on record by the defendants taking various preliminary objections therein such as that the suit of the plaintiff is a gross abuse of process of law; that the plaintiff has concealed the material facts from this court and that this court has no territorial jurisdiction to entertain and try the present suit. It has been further stated that the orders for supply of the goods were placed from Jaipur and the goods were supplied at Jaipur. It has CS DJ 58498/2016 M/s Jupitor Polytex(India) Pvt. Ltd. Vs. M/s Lotus Dairy Products Pvt. Ltd. Page No. 3 of 18 been further stated that the entire cause of action has arisen at Jaipur and not at Delhi.
texts.arguments: 6. In the brief background of facts, the defendants have stated that the defendant no. 1 is engaged in the production and supply of dairy products; that around April 2011 the official of the plaintiff approached the defendant at Jaipur and introduced the plaintiff to be a company engaged in the manufacture and supply of multi- layer films for packaging of the products and that the parties entered into three separate and independent contracts on different occasions. It has been further stated that the first oral contract was entered into in the first week of April 2011 at Jaipur for supply of 500 Kg of multi layer films to the defendant plant at Bassi, Jaipur. It has been further stated that it was expressly agreed between the parties that the purchase order was subject to the design, quality and printing to be approved by the defendant and that the acceptance of the consignment was subject to the quality tests to be carried out in the presence of the plaintiff at the Bassi plant of the defendant. It has been further stated that in pursuance to the first contract, the plaintiff supplied 484.1 Kg of multi layer films to the defendant vide invoice no. 019 dated 27.04.2011 for a sum of Rs. It has been further stated that on the basis of the price catalogue dated 07.06.2011, the defendant no. 1 vide email dated 10.06.2011, placed an order for supply of 1,000 Kg of multi layer films and the plaintiff sent a consignment of 979.8 Kg of CS DJ 58498/2016 M/s Jupitor Polytex(India) Pvt. Ltd. Vs. M / s Lotus Dairy Products Pvt. Ltd. Page No. 4 of 18 multi layer films at the defendant's plant at Bassi, Jaipur vide invoice no. 077 dated 05.07.2011 for a sum of Rs. 1,08,221/-. 7. The defendant, in the written statement, has further stated that the official of the plaintiff however failed to accompany the above said consignments for conducting the quality tests and even the earlier consignment of 484.1 Kg of multi layer films was lying unused at the Bassi plant for want of quality check. It has been further stated that the plaintiff requested the defendant for a large order of multi layer films because it was not economically viable for the plaintiff to send its representative to Jaipur for quality checkup for small quantities of the materials supplied. It has been further stated that the defendant no. 1 company placed a formal purchase order vide email dated 09.09.2011 for supply of 2,000 Kg of multi layer films of 50 micron and the plaintiff sent the consignment on 29.09.2011 for 1,989 Kg of multi layer films vide invoice bearing no. 176 dated 26.09.2011 for Rs. 2,29,542/- despite the fact that the defendant had neither accepted the counter offer of the plaintiff nor rejected the same for increase of the price vide the email dated 10.09.2011 of the plaintiff. The defendants have alleged that despite numerous reminders, the plaintiff did not send any of its officials for quality checkup and a total of 3452.9 Kgs of multi layer films supplied by the plaintiff on different occasions was lying unused in the warehouse of the defendant. It has been further stated that on account of the limited warehouse CS DJ 58498/2016 M/s Jupitor Polytex(India) Pvt. Ltd. Vs. M/s Lotus Dairy Products Pvt. Ltd. Page No. 5 of 18 space, the defendant decided to test the quality of the multi layer films in the absence of the plaintiff. The defendants have alleged that upon running the multi layer films, it was found that it had heavy leakage and pin sized holes in them. It has been further stated that the plaintiff was immediately informed vide email dated 05.10.2011 and the plaintiff was asked to send its representative to see the state of affairs and to take back the material at the earliest possible. It has been further stated that the representative of the plaintiff visited the plant on 12.10.2011 and carried the test with a small role of multi layer films by running it on the machine. It has been further stated that even the representative of the plaintiff found that there was heavy leakage. It has been alleged that despite the assurance by the representative of the plaintiff, the plaintiff failed to take back the consignments. The defendants have alleged that vide email dated 01.11.2011, the plaintiff requested for release of the payments in respect of the defective goods. The defendants have alleged that the plaintiff wanted to force the defendants to make the payment for the defective consignments of the goods and as such, it cleverly wrote mails to the defendants referring therein that there was some understanding in between the parties to the present suit but the contents of the email were totally false. On merits as well, the defendants have reiterated their above said stand. The defendants have admitted that vide three invoices dated 27.04.2011, 05.07.2011 and 26.09.2011, the goods were sent by the plaintiff to the defendant company but the defendants have taken the stand that the goods were defective and that the said plea was acknowledged by the plaintiff vide email dated 13.10.2011. The defendants have denied that they are liable to pay any amount to the plaintiff. The defendants have prayed that the suit of the plaintiff be dismissed. 12. Now coming to the evidence, the plaintiff company has examined Sh. Vijender Singhal, its director as PW1 and in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1 has further stated that on checking the roles, it was found that the leakage was within the norms of the industry. PW1 has denied the suggestion that on account of the defective goods, the defendant had to suffer a loss of Rs. 3,76,366/-.
